pc_new: Host and Container Defenders cover Linux and Windows VMs and bare metal
quote: Defender runs as a systemd service on Linux and a Windows service on Windows.
notes: Windows caveat from https://docs.prismacloud.io/admin-guide/install/deploy-defender/host/windows-host feature matrix: Windows Server 2016 and 2019 Host Defender have Yes for vulnerability, compliance and WAAS but No for runtime processes, network and filesystem. Windows Server 2019 Container Defender has runtime Processes only. Linux hosts have full runtime. Host Defender must not run beside Container Defender on the same host. Serverless and App-Embedded Defenders also exist. The Enterprise-era cell implied runtime parity on Windows hosts.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). Linux VM and bare metal sensors run in systemd mode (docs/faqs/runtime-security.md) and docs/how-to/vm-security/agent-based/linux.md has an air-gapped install section.

pc_new: Learned models plus rules with Alert, Prevent and Block effects
quote: Runtime defense is the set of features that provide both predictive and threat-based active protection for running containers.
notes: Sensors cover process, network and filesystem. Prevent stops one process (discrete blocking). Block stops the whole container. Prevent has no effect on network activity for Kubernetes attack detections. Orchestrator Defenders deploy as a DaemonSet on Kubernetes, OpenShift, GKE, ECS and TAS. Layer 4 monitoring uses iptables rules (defender-architecture page).
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). KubeArmor runtime sensors report to the on-prem control plane (docs/resources/deployment.md).

pc_new: Prevent effect stops only the violating process. Block stops the container
quote: Prevent just the discrete process or file system write (not the entire container).
notes: Limits stated in the same page: Prevent is not supported on Debian 8 or for network activities. Filesystem Prevent needs Linux kernel 4.20 or later and a storage driver other than aufs, otherwise it falls back to an alert. For new files, the binary-content detections can only alert. Enforcement is by Defender in user space, not by a named LSM. Defender fails open by design (60 second runC shim timeout on the defender-architecture page). The OPA admission webhook default failurePolicy is Ignore.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). Inline LSM enforcement runs in the KubeArmor sensor on the node (docs/faqs/runtime-security.md), so it does not depend on the control plane location.

pc_new: Scans every 24 hours by default and rescans an image when it changes
quote: By default, Prisma Cloud scans your environment every 24 hours. Images are re-scanned when changes are detected.
notes: Intervals are configurable per object type (images, containers, hosts, registries, VM images, serverless). Defender scans a new container at start and vulnerability rules can block it. An offline update path exists for a disconnected Console (https://docs.prismacloud.io/admin-guide/tools/update-intel-stream-offline says Prisma Cloud lets you update Console's vulnerability and threat data even if it runs in an offline environment). The Enterprise-era claim of several Intelligence Stream updates a day was not re-verified here.
ak_onprem_note: docs/how-to/in-cluster-image-scan-helm.md describes periodic in-cluster scans but no air-gapped vulnerability database update procedure, so confirm with engineering before the bank call.

pc_new: Allowed and denied process lists per rule, enforced with Prevent or Block
quote: Prisma Cloud runtime rules let you deny specific processes.
notes: Container rules combine the learned model (allow list) with explicit allowed and denied lists. Resultant policy is model plus allowed minus denied. Host policy supports alert or prevent processes by path and allow processes by path, and an entry in both lists is allowed.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). KubeArmor allow and deny policies apply per pod or host (docs/use-cases/app-behavior.md).

pc_new: Host FIM watches writes, reads and attributes. Container writes block by directory
quote: The Prisma Cloud FIM from Prisma Cloud continuously monitors your files and directories for changes.
notes: Host FIM rules set path, file operation and exceptions. Writes support recursive directories. Reads and attribute changes do not support recursive monitoring. The host FIM section lists monitoring and no effect field. Container filesystem rules with Prevent block file creation and modification in set directories (runtime-defense-containers page, kernel 4.20 or later). Windows hosts have no runtime filesystem support.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). docs/use-cases/vm-file-integrity.md covers VM and host paths, and the on-prem model lists VMs and bare metal on Nutanix and Linux.

pc_new: Per-image learned models enforced by rules. 1 hour learning, 24 hour dry run
quote: A model is the "allow list" for what a given container image should be doing, across all runtime sensors.
notes: Learning mode: 1 hour to build the model, then a 24 hour dry run that returns to Learning for 24 more hours if behavior changes. Models are per image digest, and per namespace and cluster in Kubernetes. Archived models are removed 24 hours after the container stops. During learning only threat-based events are logged. Extend Learning and Manual Learning are available.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). Baseline learning and block mode run in KubeArmor sensors on the cluster (docs/use-cases/zero-trust.md).

pc_new: Flags unknown and modified processes [confirm from Prisma Cloud docs]
quote: Indicates a modified process was spawned. A modified process is a process whose binary was created or modified after the container was started.
notes: No page among the 308 Compute docs names fileless or memory-only execution (grep for fileless returned 0 hits). Nearest detections: Unexpected Process (not in model), Modified Process, Temporary File System Process (hosts), Unknown Origin Binary, encrypted or packed binaries, execution flow hijack (ld.so.preload write). Keep Limited until Palo Alto Networks confirms or denies.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). The AccuKnox cell is tier A (asserted, no doc names fileless), so it carries the same confirm flag. Zero Trust allow-lists run in the node sensor (docs/use-cases/zero-trust.md).

pc_new: CIS Kubernetes node checks plus OPA admission rules that alert or block pods
quote: Rules can allow or deny (alert or block) pods.
notes: Admission rules are written in Rego by the customer. Minimum Kubernetes v1.16, no Windows support. The default ValidatingWebhookConfiguration sets failurePolicy to Ignore, so API requests continue if the webhook errors. Twistlock Labs container checks also flag root user (599), NET_RAW (596) and weak app settings (598). Findings come from Defenders, not from an agentless cluster scan.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). Cluster misconfiguration scanning is described in docs/use-cases/cluster-misconfiguration-scanning.md with no SaaS-only note.

pc_new: CIS Kubernetes, OpenShift, EKS, AKS and GKE worker node checks
quote: Prisma Cloud provides checks that validate the recommendations in the following CIS Benchmarks:
notes: EKS and AKS benchmarks are v1.2.0. GKE covers worker nodes only. OpenShift CIS needs OCP 4.6 or later and skips several checks including all of Section 5 Policies. Checks marked Not Scored are not implemented. Defaults: critical and high alert, medium and low ignore. Scan interval is 24 hours by default and configurable.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). docs/how-to/cis-benchmarking.md describes a Helm-installed scanner with a schedule and no SaaS-only note.

pc_new: Alerts on Kubernetes audit events only. No RBAC entitlement analysis
quote: Prisma Cloud can ingest, analyze, and alert on security-relevant events.
notes: Compute Edition is CWPP only (product-architecture page), so the CIEM cloud IAM analysis cited for Enterprise Edition is absent. What remains is custom and Prisma Cloud Labs rules over the Kubernetes audit stream using jpath. Audit types depend on the cluster audit policy. Istio checks cover Istio RBAC only.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). KIEM runs in the control plane against cluster RBAC data (docs/use-cases/kiem.md).

pc_new: Trusted Images rules on registry, repository and image. Alert or block
quote: If an untrusted image runs, Prisma Cloud emits an audit, raises an alert, and optionally blocks the container from running.
notes: Trusted Images is disabled by default and the default rule only alerts. Rules match by cluster or hostname, top down, first match wins. The check runs when a container starts, so it acts at runtime, not at the API admission step. OPA admission control can also deny pods.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). KnoxGuard admission rules are described in docs/use-cases/admission-controller-knoxguard.md.

pc_new: Linux Defender runs in user space, not as a kernel module. eBPF is not named
quote: Defender instead runs as a systemd or system module (not a kernel module) in user space, intercepting every syscall interaction and file changes, and actively blocking or alerting according to the rules defined in Console.
notes: No page among the 308 Compute docs contains eBPF or BPF (grep returned 0 hits). Container Defender uses Linux capabilities (net_admin, sys_admin, sys_ptrace, mknod, setfcap) and not --privileged, and layer 4 monitoring uses iptables (defender-architecture page). Windows Defender uses Windows drivers. SELinux appears only as a compatibility note. Do not claim Prisma lacks enforcement: it prevents and blocks without eBPF. Radar network monitoring needs kernel 5.4 or later if the host runs 4.15.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the On-Premises and Air-Gapped models support all features except AI CoPilot (AskADA). The on-prem model names KubeArmor runtime sensors built on eBPF (docs/resources/deployment.md).
